why: The brief sets it so: the bypass is SCAFFOLDING, not a fix. E29 demonstrates no edge, proposes no candidate, and kills none. The gate file exists so the record says that explicitly rather than leaving a fix gate unanswered.

candidates_still_killed.note: E29 re-proposes none of them and re-opens none of them.

what_E29_does_NOT_claim: It does not claim the movie path is fixed. Three movies were SKIPPED, not played.
It does not claim to know why the host stalls: streamEnded is set by fiat above the wait guard, so the nonStreamDeliveries latch E27 named is neither exercised nor disproved.
It does not claim menu/race was reached. The pre-registered C3 bar MISSED. What the boot reached is the TITLE SCREEN, read off the frame capture.

E30_handoff.headline: E29 converts E27/E28's static diagnosis into a measured cost: the single waitExternal at MPEG.cpp:2514 is the ONLY thing between the current park and a rendered, live SSX 3 title screen. Nothing else in the boot chain had to change -- one env-gated block, 46 inserted lines, zero deletions.
what_the_faithful_fix_must_reproduce_WIT: 1. getMpegPicture must RETURN to the guest instead of parking thread 1 forever. Measured: with the park suppressed, thread 1 goes from "Waiting wait=Mpeg:0 pc=0x3b1028" to "Ready", the boot log grows from 46,906 lines to 133,619, and the HLE stub surface goes from 13 distinct entry points to 251.

2. It must do so per movie, repeatedly. e29b shows the sequencer running THREE movies (feeds of 5,040 / 5,008 / 5,008 B), each arming the bypass exactly once (n=1), because sceMpegCreate resets the playback state between them. A fix that works once and latches is not enough.

3. It must keep the five tests the flag breaks GREEN: MPEG non-stream R1, R2, R4, R6 and "sceMpegGetPicture waits for new decoder output instead of duplicating the last frame". Those five are the measured regression bar -- with PS2X_SKIP_MOVIE=1 the suite is 453/458, with it off 458/458.

4. It must deliver actual pictures. Across all three movies the parser reports parseCalls=3 offered=15056 consumed=15056 packets=0 frames=0 errors=0 pending=0: every byte was consumed and NOT ONE packet completed. The bypass steps around that; a faithful fix cannot. This is the same zero-packet result E22-E28 saw on one chunk, now reproduced on three independent movies.
what_E29_hands_E30_that_it_did_not_have: A binary and a branch (e29-movie-bypass @ e5ce086d, one commit on 3adc0478) that reach the title screen, so a candidate fix can be A/B-ed against a KNOWN-REACHABLE downstream state instead of against a black screen.
The measurement that the post-movie chain is healthy: 251 distinct HLE stubs, 1,135 distinct frame contents, still changing at the wall. Whatever is wrong is in the movie delivery, not behind it.
A cheap, decisive A/B harness: the SAME binary with one env var, so any downstream difference is attributable to the wait and nothing else.
E30_handoff.the_next_question_E29_could_not_answer: Whether the title screen is polling the pad. It CANNOT be read from this boot: the [diag:stub] histogram caps at 30 rows of 251 distinct targets, and the [padread] marker only prints when a button is actually pressed, which never happened in a headless run. The runtime already has PS2X_PAD_STIM_AFTER / PS2X_PAD_STIM_WALLMIN for exactly this. One boot with START injected would settle whether "Press START button" is live -- and that is a brief to write, not a claim to make here.
